children: U.S. soybean export inspections fell from the prior week, and roughly cut in half from this time last year.

In its latest report published Monday, the Agriculture Department said that soybean export inspections totaled 250,801 metric tons for the week ended Aug. 27. That's off from 430,079 tons reported for this time last week, as well as 491,966 tons at this time last year.

Wheat inspections landed at 430,925 tons this week. That's down slightly from the previous week's 432,538 tons, but off by roughly half of what was recorded at this time last year at 804,913 tons. Corn inspections totaled nearly 1.5 million tons, up from 1.32 million tons from the prior week and 1.41 million tons at this time last year.
CBOT grain futures are mostly lower in trading Monday, with the most-active corn contract down 0.1%, soybeans up 0.1%, and wheat down 2.5%.
To see related data, search "USDA Grain Inspections for Export in Metric Tons" in Dow Jones NewsPlus.
